nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $M$ a commutative monoid and $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to M$ a function. A column is a finite list of entries from $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$; for each $j$ in this range let $c_j$ be the number of times $j$ occurs in the column. The weight of the column is the product $\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} f(c_j)$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Column weight

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a commutative monoid and $f : \mathbb{N} \to M$. The weight of an even $k \times n$ table $t$ with respect to $f$ is the product of the column weights of its $n$ columns with respect to $f$:
nodes.title: Weight of an even table

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, an even $k \times n$ table is a $k \times n$ array of entries from $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $k$ is even, every row is a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and in every column each value that occurs there occurs an even number of times.
nodes.title: Even table
